segments.text: Welcome to BxLens. Observability for BoxLang, built for the developer who has a ticket, and needs the cause. This is the demo application. Everything you are about to see is real.
The demo is a small shop with a control panel. Every page creates one kind of problem, so there is always something to find.
Start with the bar. It sits on every page, and answers one question. What happened in this request?
The strip shows the status, the time, the memory, and the queries. Open it, and the timeline lays out every template and every query, with exact timings.
Here is a classic mistake. Ten orders, eleven queries. The queries tab lists the repeated statement, and the exact line that ran it.
Outgoing calls fail in many ways. A timeout, a rate limit, a gateway error, a host that does not exist. Each one is listed, with its status and its time.
The request tab shows what this one request cost. The processor time, and the memory it allocated.
A caught exception still counts. The bar opens on the problem, by itself.
Now the console. One page for the whole server. The overview shows requests, errors, response time, and what needs your attention first.
At the top, the servers. This one is live. Two more are saved in their own folders. One of them is struggling, with high heap, failing tasks, and a deadlock.
Every request is kept. This checkout is slow, and the issues list explains why. A repeated query, and a slow outgoing call.
The same list carries security notes. Missing headers, and cookies without safe flags.
Errors are grouped by cause, with counts, and a sample with its stack. Secrets are removed before anything is stored.
Reports give the percentiles, the status codes, and the slowest addresses.
Now the runtime. This pool is saturated. Two threads, a growing queue, and health notes that say what to change.
Scheduled tasks. One is failing, with its error and its stack. One is slow, and one overlaps itself.
Datasources. Every connection is held, and the next query has to wait.
A deadlock. The JVM page flags two stuck threads, and the Threads tab shows exactly where each one is waiting.
Then the AI page. Five agents, running on a mock model. Runs, success, tokens and cost. A failing tool is flagged, with the agent that uses it.
Open the coordinator, and see how it is composed. Open a run, and the trace nests the sub agents, each tool, and each model call.
The server selector looks at any server, or at all of them at once, with the numbers added up.
Back in the demo, three support tickets. A slow checkout. Payments that fail one time in four. A site that slows down over time. Each one has a reproduce button, and BxLens has the answer.
Take the payments ticket. Reproduce it, and the errors page shows one new group. About a quarter of the requests, and the gateway's answer in the sample.
There are file watchers, and a real ColdBox application with its own schedulers. All of it, wired to the same console.
BxLens. Find the cause, not just the symptom. Install it from ForgeBox, and run this demo yourself.
